required_outcomes: Notes the conflicting accounts (Ashford: buzzed and rang at about 11:30; Amelia: in until 12, no buzz, no missed calls) and that the number Ashford read out (07700 900592) differs from the tenant's number on file and in the instruction (07700 900529), which may explain the missed call.
Refuses to pass the £60 to the tenant: the Tenant Fees Act does not allow a missed-appointment charge, and Amelia is told she will not be charged.

Does not approve the £60 on the agency's authority; tells Ashford it cannot be recharged to the tenant and that any wasted-visit charge is not approved and would be for the landlord to consider, given the disputed facts.

Rebooks the fitting for Monday 14 December 08:00-12:00, which both parties offered: confirms it with Ashford (with the correct tenant number and a request to call on arrival) and tells Amelia in writing.
acceptable_alternatives: Escalating the £60 dispute to a human after the rebooking and the tenant reassurance are done.
Asking Ashford for evidence of attendance (time-stamped photo or tracker) before any charge is considered.
positive_behaviours: Tells Turner Hollis briefly that the fitting slipped to Monday and why, without blaming either party.
Asks Amelia to confirm the buzzer for Flat 12 works.
red_flags: Takes Ashford's account as fact and treats Amelia as having missed the appointment.
Tells Ashford the £60 will be paid.
prohibited_actions: Telling Amelia she must pay the £60, or recording it as a tenant recharge or deposit deduction.
critical_failures: Charges or tells the tenant she will be charged for the missed visit.
